title: Cookie Jar
body:
The browser's local store of [[Cookies]] — a text file (or small database) on the [[Client]]'s machine, organised by domain. When a request is about to be sent, the browser looks in the jar for cookies matching that domain and path and attaches them to the `Cookie` header automatically, with no involvement from your JavaScript.

Cookies land in the jar via a `Set-Cookie` response header and stay there until they expire or are cleared. A [[Persistent Cookie]] survives a browser restart; a [[Session Cookie]] does not — session cookies and expired cookies are purged when the browser restarts.

Because the jar is a file on the user's own machine, its contents can be read and edited by the user. This is the fundamental reason cookies must be treated as untrusted user input on arrival.
